beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano makes and sells specialty chemicals in four broad categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM) and Hard Minerals (HM). These are used in paints, plastics, rubber, adhesives, cosmetics, construction and other industries.

The company does not sell directly to end-users. It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell products through the promoter's network. This dependence is acknowledged as a key competitive strength.

Customers: The top 10 customers accounted for about 59% of revenue from operations in each of FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017. The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka, with cumulative exports of ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

beats.beat: Promoters: Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (corporate promoter). Together they hold 89,48,270 equity shares, which is 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.
Promoter group (excluding promoters) holds only 21,510 shares (0.24%). Post-issue, promoter holding will dilute but the exact amount depends on the issue size (not disclosed).

Related party transactions: The company has entered into related party transactions in each of the last five financial years, as per Accounting Standard 18. These are detailed on page 223 of the DRHP.

Statutory non-compliances: Past instances of non-filing or delayed filing with the Registrar of Companies, and certain statutory licenses are yet to be obtained for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia.

The company does not own the premises for its manufacturing facilities in Tamil Nadu and administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur. It also has contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh as of September 30, 2017.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals segment was estimated at ₹1,443 billion in FY2017 and had grown at 10-12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017, with CRISIL forecasting 12-14% CAGR going forward.

Demand is driven by increased consumption, urbanisation (urban population expected to reach 36% by 2020), higher FDI (grew at 18% CAGR to $43.5 billion in FY2016), and policy support like the Draft National Chemical Policy and 100% FDI allowance.
The industry is highly fragmented – SMEs hold 70-75% market share – but only a few Indian players compete globally on product development. Import substitution is a stated opportunity.
Key sub-segments relevant to the company: construction chemicals (15% CAGR), polymer additives (10% CAGR), personal care ingredients (15% CAGR) and paints (₹401 billion market in FY2017).
The filing notes headwinds: stricter environmental regulations in China have reduced output, benefiting Indian players; but REACH compliance for exports to Europe remains a regulatory challenge.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals – functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals and hard minerals – to industries such as paints, plastics, cosmetics and construction.

The company is raising funds through an initial public offering on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to set up a new manufacturing facility in Vadodara, for general corporate purposes, and to create a public market for its shares.
The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who is 20 Microns Nano Minerals, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares (no offer for sale). The specific number of shares and price band are not disclosed in the extracts. The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

Proceeds will be used for: (i) funding capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, (ii) general corporate purposes, and (iii) creating a public trading market for the equity shares by listing on NSE EMERGE to enhance visibility and brand.

beats.beat: 1. No long-term contracts with customers or suppliers. Sales depend on purchase orders and raw material is bought on a spot basis. Loss of a key order or price spike could hurt revenue and margins.
2. Negative cash flows in the past. The company had negative operating cash flow of ₹349.75 lakh in FY2014. Sustained negative cash flow could limit growth and require additional borrowing.

3. Missing statutory licenses for a manufacturing facility. The company has not obtained all required approvals for its facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia. Non-compliance could lead to penalties or disruption.

4. Heavy reliance on the corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, for marketing and sales. Any disruption in this arrangement would materially affect operations, as the company lacks its own distribution network.
5. Related party transactions and past compliance lapses. The company has a history of related party deals and statutory filing delays, raising governance concerns for a retail investor.
